_schema.description: Feature-set identifier registry. A feature set is identified by `<compute>@w<layout>/<era>#<slots-hash8>` — see docs/FEATURE_SET_IDS.md. Counts (156 / 372 / 720 / 924 / 944 / '156+free' / '+classC') are LEGACY ALIASES, kept here so historical artifacts resolve, never as identities: '944' alone has named seven different feature sets in this repo. APPEND-ONLY: supersede with a new entry + `superseded_by`, never edit or delete one. The grammar and the hash have ONE owner, `zensim::feature_set_id`; nothing here is re-derived off-Rust.

sections.compute_tokens: The CLOSED vocabulary. token -> {slots (at 4 scales, in the widest layout), owner (the zensim symbol that decides it), note}. A token names a family whose PRESENCE changes which slots are populated. Sub-toggles (gradient / blockiness / transducer_bank / append2_dst_activity) are deliberately NOT tokens: they reshape a family from the inside, which moves the populated set, which moves the hash — so they cannot collide, and the short form stays readable.
sections.eras: token -> {build_commit, root, label, note}. The era is load-bearing: the shift between two eras of the SAME compute set is model-specific, not a constant offset (benchmarks/eval372_current_root_2026-08-30.md), so a number read on one era cannot be corrected into the other, only re-verdicted.
sections.sets: id -> the registered feature set. `kind`:'set' is fully pinned (has `slots` + `slots_hash8`, both checked against the owner by zensim-validate's registry test); `kind`:'class' pins compute+layout+era only, for a MODEL class whose exact read-set differs per bake (the name is the class, the hash is the instance). `role`:'producer' populates those slots; 'consumer' reads them.
sections.roots: absolute features-root path -> set id, for inferring a PRODUCER id from a root that predates the `feature_set_id` manifest key. An inferred id is evidence about the artifact's NAME, never about its BYTES, and consumers must badge it.
sections.regime_strings: the prose `regime` string a `_MANIFEST.json` already carries -> the compute+slots it implies, so a root with no `feature_set_id` key still resolves. A regime string that varies PER FILE inside one root (wlin7b-2026-08-30: 'mixed by file: *_pools944 = folded720append2pools, *_ctrl944 = folded720append2') resolves to null — mixed roots must be addressed per file.
sections.aliases: legacy name -> list of ids it has meant. A list of length > 1 is AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION and a consumer must say so rather than pick one.

entry_fields.slots: compact canonical slot ranges, e.g. '0-155,720-923' (kind='set' only)
entry_fields.slots_hash8: 8 lowercase hex of zensim::feature_set_id::slots_hash8 over `slots` (kind='set' only)
entry_fields.n_slots: |slots| — redundant with `slots`, carried so a reader can sanity-check without parsing
entry_fields.evidence: the doc/record that establishes this set exists
entry_fields.superseded_by: id of the entry that replaces this one, when applicable

carriers.note: the ten fused944native carrier slots; every other pool slot stays 0

peaks.note: v1 soft-peak pool; costs the same as Off — the accumulators are unconditional

masked.note: v1 masked pool; separate token from `iw` because a bake can read one without the other

append.note: append-204; owns GLOBAL_* when it runs

append2.note: append2/BANDVIS; owns LUMA_MEAN_REF when it runs

csfw.note: CSFW tier-1, Y-only; default-OFF, no canonical root yet

moments.note: 37 scattered slots a v1-only walk finalizes for free; named ONLY when the owning block is off (ComputeSet::raw_moments) — benchmarks/free_features_2026-09-01.md §1

classc.note: 24 scattered slots at EXISTING 944 positions — 12 v2 MSE + 12 Y-channel luminance-bin; ~1.3-2.3% of the 156 walk, NOT free — benchmarks/free_features_classC_2026-09-04.md

v1postc_rev2.label: post-option-C 372 at zensim FORMULA REVISION 2 (ZENSIM_FORMULA_REV=2)
v1postc_rev2.note: Same extractor build class as v1postc, one formula revision later. Revision 2 declares three eras -- v1ssimcap (F4, arm Clamp), freecomp (F5) and v1hfgain (F17, arm SaturatingExcess). At width 372 freecomp is UNREACHABLE (it needs an append block) and Clamp moves ZERO cells on every corpus this box has pixels for, so the only observable change from v1postc is F17 on the twelve contrast_inc slots f12,25,38,51,64,77,90,103,116,129,142,155. MEASURED, not derived: the fleet executor at rev2 is BIT-EXACT to the R6b lane's `satexcess` arm on csiq/tid/konjnd/live/kadid/aic3 (6,092,616 cells, 0 differ), through a different code path. Decoder era is ALL-IMAZEN (zenmetrics-cli/src/decode.rs at master 4d9629500c53), which differs from v1postc's cid22 leg -- see the cid22 note below.
v1postc_rev2.produced_by: zenfleet JobKind::Feature, run s3://zentrain/jobs/rev2feat372-20260906, image ghcr.io/imazen/zenfleet-worker:exec-featrev2glibc-88477e38 (glibc, on purpose)
v1postc_rev2.cid22_decoder_caveat: v1postc's cid22/kadid/tid/pipal legs come from `zensim-validate --extract-only`, which decodes with the third-party `image` crate (main.rs:830/854/1720/1744). This root decodes with the imazen codecs, so its cid22 differs from v1postc's on EXACTLY the 536 .jpg rows of 4,292 (100 % of jpg, 0 % of png), ~360 of 372 slots each, max |delta| 9.5e-3. kadid (png) and tid (bmp) are bit-exact because both decoders give identical pixels there.
v1postc_rev2.libc_caveat: Built with GLIBC deliberately. The musl build of the same source differs on the 144 L4/L8 pooled-moment slots -- powf is not correctly rounded and musl's pow disagrees with glibc's on 0.069 % of inputs (glibc 2.36 vs 2.43 measured bit-identical on 400,000 samples). Record: benchmarks/libm_pow_nondeterminism_2026-09-06.md.

era2r4_rev2.label: era2r4 944 (folded720append2) at zensim FORMULA REVISION 2
era2r4_rev2.note: The 944 counterpart of v1postc_rev2. Here freecomp (F5) IS reachable -- the append block exists -- so all THREE revision-2 eras are live, and the blast radius is F4's 36 zeroed-pool slots + F17's 12 + F5's 11, not the 372 root's 12. Produced by the same fleet run family (s3://zentrain/jobs/rev2feat944-20260906) over the SAME staged pixels as v1postc_rev2, so the two roots are joinable row-for-row per corpus.

basic+peaks+masked+iw+v2+append+append2+.evidence: feature_v2::FeatureRegime::Folded720Csfw — default-OFF, no canonical root yet

basic+peaks+moments@w944/era2r4#0b476506.evidence: scripts/sota944/slice_basic156_free_nolumaref.txt — the 265 set MINUS f926/931/936/941 (LUMA_MEAN_REF, one per scale). MEASURED (benchmarks/fastclass2_campaign_2026-09-05.md §0a, on the 39-row 944-pools identity probe): those four are the ONLY slots in the 265 set whose ref==dist value exceeds 4.8e-3, at max |v| 0.688 / spread 0.261 — LUMA_MEAN_REF is the free set's only reference-absolute statistic, so it cannot vanish at identity.
basic+peaks+moments@w944/era2r4#0b476506.note: SAME handle as its producer and a DIFFERENT hash: this is a READER subset — the walk (V1PoolsMode::Peaks + V1FreeExtras::RawMoments) still emits all 37 moment slots, the model reads 33 of them, and dead-column pruning drops the four lines at pack time. That is the designed case for `the name is a handle and the hash is the identity` (docs/FEATURE_SET_IDS.md); the key carries the hash so the two entries cannot be confused. Registry lookups are by key, never by (compute,layout,era), so the shared triple is not a collision.
